text: The per-service login of rwb-decision has no name in any source. This story refers to it as the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and never to the monolith login.
why: R5 fixes one login per service and DP-02 repeats it, but no source names the login of this service.
read: R5 service naming; DP-02; TSD P7 T6.2
confirm: The ACE DB owner who creates the schema and the login (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB)
impact: Naming only: no column, key, index or scenario changes if the name differs.

text: The migration file of this story is V<seq>__rwb_p7_e1001_decision_schema.sql, line 1 carries the story key RWB-P7-E1001-APP, and its four-digit sequence is taken in merge order under the naming rule of D-RCV-28.
why: D-RCV-28 fixes the file naming pattern and the merge-order sequence but names no file for this story.
confirm: The rwb-decision tech lead at merge
impact: The file name and its number only; no object, column or scenario changes.

text: The constraint and index names follow the platform naming convention, and each read index leads with the column section 13 names for its path; the remaining column order and every name are agreed at merge.
why: No source names a constraint or an index of these six tables, and the read paths need one leading column each.
read: TSD P7 T3.1 and T3.3; R5.5 DP-15
confirm: The rwb-decision tech lead and the plan check owner
impact: Names and secondary column order only; the plans of AC10 depend on the leading columns, which are fixed.

text: approval.case_id and approval.delegation_limit_id are values with no foreign key, although TSD P7 T3.3 and the LDM relationships sheet name them as foreign keys to recovery_case and delegation_limit: under DP-01 no foreign key crosses a schema, and the owners of those tables are rwb_case (P3) and rwb_access (P4).
why: The specification declares the two keys against tables that live in two other services after the split, and DP-01 forbids a cross-schema key.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01; Ownership Map rows of the context pack P7
confirm: The solution architect and the data owners of rwb_case and rwb_access
impact: The schema keeps five foreign keys inside rwb_decision and no join to another schema; a referential check of the case and the limit row moves to the caller.

text: The 7 standard columns of TSD P7 T3.0 carry no Field IDs in the sources; they are carried by the one dictionary seed of RWB-P1-E1001-APP, and this story declares and cites only the business Field IDs of its six tables.
why: TSD P7 T3.0 lists the standard columns with types only, and the LDM fields sheet names no Field ID for them.
read: TSD P7 T3.0; LDM fields sheet
confirm: RWB-P1-E1001-APP as the owner of the dictionary
impact: The declaration covers the business fields and ignores the standard columns in both directions; no column changes.

text: The six platform contracts of the DP table (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are carried in the preconditions and in CG-B2-P7-001-1 rather than in an H row, because the metadata row of this secondary slice is None and its Ready to start is Day 1.
why: The DP table adds those H dependencies, while the work package fixes Depends on (build) as None for this slice and the contracts are already build dependencies of the service baseline.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP table; R5.7 lane rules; the WP story line for RWB-P7-E1001-APP
impact: The story starts on Day 1 against the service baseline and its fakes; no lane depth and no build order changes.

text: This story declares its field rows as a build artefact, hands them to the one dictionary seed of RWB-P1-E1001-APP, proves them matched by a conformance test, writes no sys_fields, sys_objects or data_product row and reads no rwb_source_data table at run time.
why: One dictionary over 14 data products and 122 objects cannot be split, and a read of rwb_source_data from rwb-decision would be a cross-schema read under DP-01.
read: Ownership Map rows of the context pack P7; FSD P1; DP-01; R3 default ruling
impact: The dictionary stays single and is seeded by its owner; the conformance test fails the build if the declaration and the columns drift.

text: rule_row is built with the 21 fields its fields sheet lists (DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015, DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054 and DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298), and not with the 18 its entity sheet states.
why: The same LDM disagrees with itself; the fields sheet is the row-level definition the declaration and the conformance test read.
read: LDM entity sheet and fields sheet
confirm: The solution architect who owns the LDM
impact: Three columns (package_version_id, drools_rule_name and outputs) exist in rwb_decision that the entity sheet count does not reflect; no scenario changes.

text: rule_test_case.package_version_id, named only by the LDM relationships sheet, is not created: a test case names its rule by rule_id and rule_version and its version through rule_row, which holds package_version_id.
why: The fields sheet of rule_test_case defines no such column, and a column with no Field ID cannot be declared to the one dictionary.
read: LDM fields sheet and relationships sheet; TSD P7 T3.1
confirm: The solution architect who owns the LDM
impact: One column fewer than the relationships sheet implies; the rule-registry stories read the version through rule_row.
